subject: Career
title: Remote Work and Career Advancement
description: A fast breakdown of Remote Work and Career Advancement for builders.

hook.text: Remote workers are 38% less likely to receive a bonus and 35% less likely to be promoted. The visibility penalty is real.

buildup.text: Out of sight, out of mind isn't just a saying. Proximity to decision-makers correlates with advancement.

discovery.text: The fix isn't going back to the office. It's making your impact visible through proactive communication.

twist.text: Self-promotion feels uncomfortable. But sharing your wins isn't bragging — it's informing.

climax.text: Weekly visibility tactics: share wins in team channels, present at all-hands, and schedule 1:1s with leadership.

punchline.text: Remote success requires making invisible work visible.

quiz.question: How much less likely are remote workers to receive a bonus?

details.summary: Remote workers face a visibility gap that can slow career advancement compared to in-office peers. Proactive self-advocacy, documented accomplishments, and strategic visibility ensure that distributed work does not become career-limiting.
details.whyItMatters: Proximity bias in promotion decisions is well-documented. Remote workers who do not actively manage their visibility may produce excellent work that goes unrecognized by decision-makers.
takeaways: Document and share your accomplishments proactively with leadership
Seek high-visibility projects and volunteer for cross-team initiatives
Schedule regular one-on-ones with your manager focused on growth

faq.question: Do remote workers get promoted less frequently than their in-office peers?
faq.answer: Studies suggest they can if they do not actively manage their visibility. The work quality may be equal, but in-office workers benefit from spontaneous interactions with leadership. Remote workers must create their own visibility through proactive communication and strategic self-advocacy.

faq.question: What is the best way to increase your visibility as a remote worker?
faq.answer: Send concise weekly updates to your manager highlighting accomplishments and impact. Volunteer for presentations and cross-functional projects. Build relationships with stakeholders outside your immediate team through virtual coffee chats. Make your contributions impossible to overlook.
